title: HOS Commands 0.2 policy profile
description: Draft. The minimal policy HOS Commands 0.2 requires: an allow list of permissions for one tenant, in which anything not permitted is refused. A permission names a command type, the requesters it admits, and a mode: recommend, where a command is proposed and never executed, or approve_and_run, where a person with an admitted role approves and the command is executed. In 0.2 nothing is executed without a human approval. The profile uses the terms of the PRD (tenant, actor, action, target, preconditions, approver role, expiry) so that Trust 0.3 extends it rather than replaces it: a portable policy language, general thresholds and limits, and bounded autonomy are not part of 0.2.

hospolicyversion.description: HOS version the policy conforms to. A document with this member is a policy.

version.description: The version of the policy. A command and an approval record the version they were evaluated against.

properties.description: The properties of the tenant the policy covers.

permissions.description: What is permitted. A command no permission covers is refused: an empty list refuses everything.

properties.description: The properties the permission covers; absent, all those of the policy.

mode.description: recommend: the command is proposed and stays proposed until it expires or is cancelled. approve_and_run: it goes to approval, then runs.

requesters.description: Who may propose the command: a pseudonymous reference, or user:* or integration:* for any requester of that kind.

approver_roles.description: The roles of the tenant that may approve the command.

allow_self_approval.description: Whether the requester may approve their own command. Absent means false.

command_validity_seconds.description: The longest a command may live between its request and its expiry.

approval_validity_seconds.description: The longest an approval may live between the decision and its expiry.

required_preconditions.description: The kinds of precondition a command must carry on top of those its type requires.

max_per_hour.description: The most commands of this type that may be proposed for the tenant in an hour.

max_per_target_per_day.description: The most commands of this type that may target the same entity in a day.
